newsitem.title: AZERBAIJAN: Azeris urge Russia's Rosneft to join oil projects.
newsitem.headline: Azeris urge Russia's Rosneft to join oil projects.

text.p: Russia's state-owned oil company Rosneft should participate in oil projects in Azerbaijan, Azeri President Haydar Aliyev said on Tuesday.
Aliyev met with a delegation of Rosneft representatives headed by company chairman Alexander Putilovthis week.
"The participation of Russian companies in joint oil structures in the Azeri section of the Caspian Sea would be useful and necessary," Aliyev said.
He said he received a letter from Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin recommending Rosneft, and ordered a plan for concrete cooperation be drawn up in the near future.
Natik Aliyev, president of Azerbaijan's state oil company SOCAR, said a working group with Rosneft would be set up and determine within two months how the companies would work together.
Putilov said Rosneft had worked with fellow Russian oil major LUKoil on seismic studies in the Caspian, and could join well projects in Azerbaijan.
Putilov was sacked as chairman and president of Rosneft at the end of April, but was reinstated as chairman just over a week later.
Azerbaijan has concluded five major deals worth more than $10 billion with foreign oil companies in the last few years.
But only one Russian company numbers among the foreign partners. LUKoil has a stake in three contracts and owns a chain of filling stations.
